field.label: Enable
field.help: Manage the tunnels listed below. Normally enabled. Off stops everything on this page and removes the tunnels' firewall pins and MSS clamp; the tunnels themselves keep running.

field.label: Health mirror
field.help: Hold each tunnel down while its bound WAN is down, and each IPv6 tunnel gateway down while its IPv4 tunnel is unhealthy (the IPv6 gateway's own monitor decides the rest). Normally enabled.

field.label: IPv6 addresses and routes
field.help: Keep each tunnel's IPv6 address, next-hop route and IPv6 monitor route in place (core adds no IPv6 far-gateway route). Off stops maintaining them; a tunnel restart then leaves its IPv6 gateway without routes, unmeasured and reading down. Normally enabled when any tunnel has IPv6.

field.label: Default-route guard
field.help: Normally enabled if the router is using one or more WANs as route defaults. Removes a default route that points through a tunnel or any other non-default gateway, for both address families.

field.label: WAN pins
field.help: Block each tunnel's handshakes from leaving by any WAN other than the one its endpoint route binds it to. Normally enabled; off removes these firewall rules.

field.label: Only NATed traffic into tunnels
field.help: Block any packet entering a tunnel from any address but that tunnel's own, i.e. traffic outbound NAT did not translate to it. Normally enabled; off removes these firewall rules.

field.label: MSS clamp
field.help: Clamp TCP MSS on each tunnel to its MTU (IPv4 MTU−40, IPv6 MTU−60), both directions. Normally enabled; it matters on WANs with a smaller path MTU, such as mobile ones.
